campbell.title: Campbell City Council — November 17, 2026
campbell.summary: The agenda for the November 17, 2026, Campbell City Council meeting listed several resolutions honoring longtime city staff, including one recognizing Chief Gary Berg's retirement after more than 32 years. It also included a temporary pause on approving detention or custodial facilities, updated building and fire codes, and a contract to design a replacement for the Community Center pool.
keyTopics: The agenda listed an urgency ordinance for a temporary moratorium on approving applications for detention facilities, custodial detention facilities, or custodial processing facilities. The moratorium would also cover establishing or operating those facilities.
The agenda listed the first reading of an ordinance re-adopting the 2025 California Building Code series and Campbell's local amendments to its fire protection and building code chapters.

The agenda listed a resolution to approve a consultant agreement with Ruhnau Clarke Architects for architectural and engineering design of the Community Center Pool Replacement Project and to authorize the City Manager to sign it.

The consent calendar listed resolutions commending Chief Gary Berg (over 32 years, retirement), Ana Rios (25 years), and Support Services Manager Andrea Atkinson (seven years, nearly 30 years in public safety).

The consent calendar also listed approval of bills and claims totaling $3,439,007.77 and the second reading of Ordinance 26-2356 for a Planned Development Permit with a Tree Removal Permit at Campbell Technology Parkway.

saratoga.title: Saratoga City Council — November 18, 2026
saratoga.summary: The agenda for the Saratoga City Council's November 18, 2026, meeting listed a public hearing on an appeal over a proposed 69-unit housing development on Quito Road, along with discussions on annexing the Mountain Winery property and handing over management of the Saratoga Civic Theater. It also included a recognition of the Scareatoga Scarecrows organizers, routine business items, a historic property tax agreement, and an update on Saratoga Village business vitality.
keyTopics: Public hearing on an appeal of the Planning Commission's denial of a 69-unit project at 14076 Quito Road (55 townhome/condominium units plus 14 attached affordable accessory dwelling units on a 3.85-acre site split into 14 lots); staff recommended upholding the appeal and conditionally approving the project
Discussion of a potential annexation of the Mountain Winery property, with Council asked to direct staff on any additional work it wants done
Proposal to authorize the City Manager's Office to transition management and operations of the Saratoga Civic Theater to South Bay Musical Theatre
Proposed Mills Act agreement (a historic property preservation contract) for 19490 Glen Una Drive, a designated landmark

Recognition of the Scareatoga Scarecrows project organizers (Laurel Perusa, Lynda Pevar, Tina Liddie and Cody Teerlink) and a Saratoga Village economic vitality update presenting ideas gathered from community engagement

los-altos.title: Los Altos City Council — October 27, 2026
los-altos.summary: The agenda for the October 27, 2026, Los Altos City Council meeting listed routine business such as contracts and equipment purchases, along with a proposed extension of a temporary moratorium on certain detention and custodial facilities. It also listed a Cal Water presentation on water conservation and a proposed salary amendment for the City Manager.
keyTopics: Proposed contract with Lignum Mellis of San Francisco to complete the Building B Park Expansion Project for up to $166,225, plus a contingency of up to 10%
Proposed $417,400 contract with ELECCO of Milpitas, plus a contingency of up to 15%, to replace the Police Department's back-up generator
Proposed extension of Ordinance No. 2026-548, a temporary moratorium related to detention or custodial facilities and custodial processing facilities
Proposed amendment to the City Manager's employment agreement setting a $375,000 annual base salary effective July 5, 2026, with a yearly CPI/general salary adjustment beginning July 2027
Cal Water presentation on water conservation measures and a proposed Transit Signal Priority Policy on behalf of VTA

los-gatos.title: Los Gatos Town Council — November 17, 2026
los-gatos.summary: The agenda for the November 17, 2026, Los Gatos Town Council meeting listed routine housekeeping items such as meeting minutes, bill and payroll approvals, and completed street work, along with a zoning code change and a proposal to add a Senior Planner position.
keyTopics: The agenda listed adoption of an ordinance amending Chapter 29 (Zoning Regulations) of the Town Code.
The agenda listed consideration of adding a full-time Senior Planner position to the Fiscal Year 2026-27 budget.

The agenda listed a request to authorize a Certificate of Acceptance and Notice of Completion for the 2026 Annual Curb, Gutter, and Sidewalk Maintenance Project. It also listed a request to authorize the Town Manager to execute a certificate of acceptance and notice of completion for another project.
The agenda listed approval of meeting minutes from the October 28, 2026, closed session and the November 2, 2026, special meeting.
The agenda listed approval and ratification of the accounts payable check registers and payroll report.

san-jose.body: Rules and Open Government Committee and Committee of the Whole
san-jose.title: San José Rules and Open Government Committee and Committee of the Whole — November 18, 2026
san-jose.summary: The agenda listed a joint session of San José's Rules and Open Government Committee and the Committee of the Whole to plan what the City Council would take up at upcoming meetings. The agenda listed the committee's review of the November 24, 2026, City Council agenda as canceled. It also listed the December 1, 2026, draft agenda for review, along with several council-sponsored community events and a proposed new cultural district.
keyTopics: The agenda listed the committee's review of the November 24, 2026, City Council agenda as canceled. It also listed the December 1, 2026, draft agenda for review, including adding new items and scheduling specific items at set times.
The agenda listed the proposed establishment of the La Avenida Cultural District, brought by Mayor Mahan and Councilmembers Ortiz, Campos, Tordillos, and Candelas.

The agenda listed retroactive approval of a Senior Symposium sponsored by Council District 9 (Foley) as a council-sponsored special event allowing city funds to be spent and donated materials and services to be accepted.
The agenda listed retroactive approval of a bus visit to the Vietnam Traveling Memorial Wall sponsored by Council District 7 (Doan), under the same special-event rules.

The agenda listed approval of a Holiday Children Book Drive proclamation and event sponsored by Council District 1 (Kamei). It also listed several events sponsored by Council District 6 (Mulcahy) for approval, some retroactively.

mountain-view.title: Mountain View Tennis Advisory Committee — November 19, 2026
mountain-view.summary: The agenda for the November 19, 2026, Mountain View Tennis Advisory Committee meeting listed routine business, including approving past minutes, planning next year's meetings, and choosing a committee chair. Residents could also address the committee during the public comment portion of the agenda.
keyTopics: The agenda listed approval of minutes from a prior meeting.
The agenda listed the 2027 meeting schedule and work plan for the committee.
The agenda listed nomination of a Tennis Advisory Committee Chair and recruitment of new members.
The agenda included a public comment period for topics outside the agenda. Each speaker could comment once for up to three minutes and could cover any number of topics.

sunnyvale.title: Sunnyvale City Council — November 17, 2026
sunnyvale.summary: The agenda for the November 17, 2026, Sunnyvale City Council meeting listed a $3.27 million contract for the second phase of the Plaza del Sol project, a proposed local emergency declaration tied to the developing El Niño event, and several items on housing and RV parking. It also listed a proposed salary and benefits change for the City Attorney.
keyTopics: The agenda listed a $3,268,600 contract with S & H Construction, Inc., for the Plaza del Sol Phase II ReBid Project, along with a 10% construction contingency ($326,860) and a budget modification of $1,067,998.
The agenda listed a resolution proclaiming a local emergency in Sunnyvale due to the developing 2026-2027 El Niño event.
The agenda listed adoption of an ordinance changing the Below Market Rate ownership housing program rules on paying an in-lieu fee to meet the affordable housing requirement.
The agenda listed a proposal to direct staff to prepare an implementation plan and begin environmental review for an Interim Housing Community at 1240 Fair Oaks Way.
The agenda listed consideration of an RV permit parking program on Caribbean Drive and a study of a possible Safe Parking pilot program at 241 Commercial Street, with a $122,000 budget modification.

cupertino.title: Cupertino City Council — November 17, 2026
cupertino.summary: The agenda for the November 17, 2026, Cupertino City Council meeting listed a closed-door legal discussion about two lawsuits against the city, a recognition of Small Business Saturday, and a consent calendar of routine items. It also listed three items on council policy: community funding and festival fee waivers, updates to the Council Procedures Manual, and council compensation.
keyTopics: The agenda listed a closed-session conference with legal counsel on two existing lawsuits: Lixin (Leon) Chen, et al. v. City of Cupertino and Yes in My Backyard, et al. v. City of Cupertino, both in Santa Clara County Superior Court.
The agenda listed a recognition of Small Business Saturday, which falls on Saturday, November 28, 2026.
The consent calendar listed a maximum rate schedule for Rate Period Seven (RP 7) for Recology's recycling, organics, and solid waste collection and processing services.

The consent calendar also listed adoption of the 2026 Emergency Operations Plan and a first amendment to the lease agreement with the Cupertino Library covering aquarium maintenance and janitorial services.

The agenda listed three council-governance items: subcommittee recommendations on the Community Funding Policy and festival fee waivers, amendments to the City Council Procedures Manual (previously postponed on May 5, 2026), and an ordinance amending Municipal Code Section 2.16.020 on City Council compensation.

santa-clara.title: Santa Clara Stevens Creek Corridor Steering Committee — November 23, 2026
santa-clara.summary: The November 23 agenda listed the meeting in the Council Chambers at San José City Hall (200 E Santa Clara St.) and offered a Zoom webinar for remote participation with advance registration. The committee oversees a joint transportation study by San José, Santa Clara, Cupertino, Santa Clara County, and VTA.
keyTopics: The agenda listed approval of the previous meeting's minutes (the January 28, 2026, meeting summary) as an action item.
The agenda listed an information item on current corridor activities.
The agenda listed an information item on 2016 Measure B Complete Streets bicycle and pedestrian improvements along the Stevens Creek corridor.
The agenda listed an information item on next steps for the corridor study.

The agenda asked the public to register to join the Zoom webinar. To speak, remote participants could raise their hand in Zoom or press *9 by phone. Speakers generally had two minutes, or twice that if they used a translator. The agenda directed people to email written comments to wilson.tam@sanjoseca.gov before or during the meeting.

milpitas.title: Milpitas City Council — November 17, 2026
milpitas.summary: The agenda for the November 17, 2026, Milpitas City Council meeting listed routine business such as meeting calendars, minutes, and the 2027 meeting schedule, along with several contract and labor items. Items before the Council included a holiday closure schedule, temporary staffing and maintenance supply contracts, added funding for homeless outreach services, and new labor agreements for two employee groups.
keyTopics: Holiday closure schedule and a resolution delegating authority to the City Manager or designee to approve and execute project-related documents and urgent administrative items during the Council's winter recess
Proposed agreements with six firms for as-requested temporary staffing, up to $1,500,000 total over five years, subject to appropriation by the City Council
Proposed amendment to add $163,522 to the WeHope contract for homeless outreach, assessment, and mobile hygiene services
Proposed agreements with 74 vendors for citywide maintenance supplies, materials, and related services over a five-year term

Successor labor agreements (July 1, 2026, through June 30, 2030) with the Milpitas Professional and Technical Group (ProTech) and the Mid-Management and Confidential Unit, plus a related FY2026-27 budget appropriation

palo-alto.title: Palo Alto City Council — November 16, 2026
palo-alto.summary: The agenda for the Palo Alto City Council's November 16, 2026, meeting listed a joint study session with the Utilities Advisory Commission on the city's water supply, along with items on housing, a creek bridge replacement, a nature preserve park project, and a rezoning on Olive Avenue. It also listed routine business such as meeting minutes, a conflict-of-interest code update, and contract amendments for the City Manager, City Attorney, and City Clerk.
keyTopics: The agenda listed a joint study session of the City Council and Utilities Advisory Commission on water-supply reliability, with presentations from city staff, the Bay Area Water Supply & Conservation Agency (BAWSCA), and the Yosemite Rivers Alliance.
The agenda listed a request to approve a $1,555,050 local matching-funds agreement with the Santa Clara Valley Water District for replacing the Newell Road/San Francisquito Creek Bridge.

The agenda listed a proposal to rezone 470 Olive Avenue from single-family residential to medium-density mixed use and add it as a housing inventory site, matching the neighboring 2951 El Camino Real parcel.
The agenda listed a proposal to issue a request for proposals and provide local funding for an affordable housing development at 340 Portage Avenue (Matadero Creek).

The agenda listed implementation of Housing Element Program 3.9(A), which aims to identify incentives that shift the economic benefit of redevelopment from commercial toward home building at strategic locations.
